evidence: Judge agent+model are set once in task.toml [verifier.env] (REWARDKIT_JUDGE="claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", OpenRouter base URL, ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}, empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), byte-identical to the template; all five judge.toml files carry only the expected judge="claude-code" fallback and no model/temperature/effort (grep for model=|temperature|effort over tests/*/*/judge.toml: no hits). tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, tools/score.py and tools/restart_mcp.py are identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template after CRLF normalisation; the Dockerfile pins @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7, express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1, and installs Chromium through the pinned @playwright/mcp's bundled playwright CLI symlinked to /usr/local/bin/chromium, which every judge.toml's playwright-mcp uses via --executable-path. Graded time rules use a fixed clock: integration.md:7 states 'The firm runs on a fixed clock, 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z ... timers are measured against it', app_context.md:29 repeats it, seed_data.json carries clock=2026-05-12T11:00:00Z, and server.js:32-33/143/418/439 derives every stored time and the sweep (CLOCK_MS - Date.parse(r.at) >= limit) from seed.clock, never Date.now(). Criteria figures are all clock-relative and agree with the seed: functional judge.toml:127 (K-10 at 2026-05-05T11:00:00Z exactly seven days -> gone; K-11 one second younger -> shown), :138-139 (K-18 3 May = nine days, K-13 4 May = eight days on a 30->7 day change), :257-258 (transcript generated 2026-05-12 11:00; Survey at 2026-05-08 15:00). The scripted golden run on 9 Oct 2026 (real date ~5 months after the fixed clock; hash-verified in raw-evidence-index) passed deleted_and_expired_messages, timer_changes, hold_scope_and_release and search_and_transcript, showing grading does not depend on the run date. Adversarial probes: a broken app using the real wall clock (Oct 2026) would expire every non-held seed message including K-11, failing the positive control at judge.toml:127-128 rather than passing; a conforming app that stores the fixed clock but formats times differently is protected by '(any clear date-time format)' wording at :257-258 and app_context.md:29. No graded criterion references 'now' in run-date terms. Open public network and missing allowlist are not defects per the workbook row and SKILL delivery profile.
notes: Base images (node:22-bookworm-slim, python:3.12-slim) are tag- not digest-pinned and apt packages are unpinned; both are template-controlled and identical to the template, so not a task defect (unpinned apt is a NOTE under the deterministic sheet). LLM judge output is inherently non-deterministic; the row only requires pinned agent/model/tools, which holds. No full configured judge run exists on these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope says so); hosted-v2 results are for earlier bytes. This row's pinning half is fully source-verifiable; the fixed-clock half is exercised by the scripted golden run, not by the judge, hence run_verdict PARTIAL. This review cannot imply any Oracle, model or portal score.
